purpose: Local corpus of real-world supply-chain datasets (SEC EDGAR 10-Ks, EM-DAT disasters, Wikipedia crisis articles, World Bank macro/pink-sheet, FRED PPI, OpenFlights, NOAA, WTO tariffs) downloaded by fetch scripts. Feeds the RAG corpora (v3 benchmarks), the EM-DAT crisis library cook (scripts/crisis_library/cook_v2.py -> crisis_library_v2.json used by the live server), and the v5 Platinum counterfactual. plots/ holds one tracked calibration PNG used by demo docs.
verdict: The raw data is the genuinely good news of this subsystem: I sampled every text-readable dataset and it is overwhelmingly REAL â€” genuine SEC XBRL 10-K filings (Workiva-stamped, 75MB), a genuine 16,811-row EM-DAT export with full 47-column schema and GADM migration metadata (Last Update 2025-12-20), real FRED PPI series, real World Bank API JSON, real OpenFlights .dat files, real Wikipedia article text, and 2 of 3 real Fed/BIS PDFs. No generated CSVs, no np.random data. But everything around the data is rotten: the entire directory is gitignored INCLUDING its own fetch script (fetch_all.py is untracked â€” a fresh clone cannot rebuild any of this); there is NO script anywhere in the repo that fetches the EM-DAT xlsx, the policy PDFs, or the world_bank_macro JSONs (provenance scripts lost); every v3_arcadia consumer resolves external_data to the wrong directory after the versions/ reorg (silent empty-glob corpora); the one "policy paper" frbny_supply_chain.pdf is actually an HTML error page saved as .pdf yet counted in receipts; R1_VERIFIED.json overcounts FRED files (claims 2, one 404'd); and the flagship "real FRED" counterfactual in platinum.py parses columns DATE/VALUE that don't exist in the CSV (actual header: observation_date,PCU484121484121), so it ALWAYS silently falls back to a hardcoded severity-to-USD table while mislabeling monthly truck-transport PPI as "FRED Brent crude daily prices". Roughly 4MB+ of downloaded data (OpenFlights, WTO zip, NOAA track, pink sheet xlsx) is consumed by nothing â€” trophy downloads padding the dataset count.
